rules.statement: Dangling and cross-tenant references do not compile; a request that reaches a Broken entry on the data plane fails closed (F4, F5).
The codecs neither encode nor decode Match.Exactly("*"): * only ever means Match.Any.
guards: document:PolicyDocumentCodecTest#the wildcard is only ever Any

rules.statement: A document whose schema is not this version's format fails to decode, as does one that is not exactly this format (an unknown field, a second operator, a value of the wrong JSON type), and the requests that need it fail closed.

A path pattern's cost is bounded: an `http:path:` pattern longer than 2,048 characters, or with a segment that mixes `*`, `?` or `{name}` with other text in more than 16 parts (consecutive `*` counting once), does not compile, nor does a document whose patterns hold more than 2,048 glob units in all: the parts and literal characters of such segments, counted twice after a leading `**` or `{*name}` and for a rate limit rule keyed by a captured variable. A typed resource pattern is at most 2,058 characters.
guards: engine:HttpPathPatternTest#a pattern is at most 2048 characters
engine:HttpPathPatternTest#a glob segment holds at most 16 tokens
engine:HttpPathPatternTest#consecutive stars in a segment count once
engine:HttpPathPatternTest#a glob after a leading rest costs twice and is tried at two starts
engine:HttpPathPatternTest#a glob after a leading rest is decided at most twice
engine:HttpPathPatternTest#capturing agrees with backtracking
engine:CompiledDocumentTest#a document holds at most its glob budget
engine:ActionResourcePatternTest#a typed pattern is at most 2058 characters

rules.statement: Every stored format CoSec reads, and every control-plane request body, refuses an object with a duplicate key: CoSec's one mapper reads them all with duplicate detection, so no value is read as whichever of two came last.
guards: cocache:StoredFormatTest#a duplicate key fails every stored format
control:ControlHttpTest#a body with a duplicate key is refused

rules.statement: A document holds at most 64 rate limit rules, whatever its kind: every rule a permitted request matches costs the pipeline one call to the rate limiter, so a document with more does not compile (a stored one is installed as failed, and the control plane answers a change with a COMPILE finding, 422).
guards: engine:CompiledDocumentTest#a document holds at most its rate limit rules

rules.source: RFC 0006 §8.1; round-2 review M3 of the backends
rules.statement: A rate limit rule's window is at most a day (windowSeconds from 1 to 86400): a counter key lives two windows in a Redis that must not evict, one key per bucket value, so a long window keyed by something a client chooses would be memory the client controls. A document with a longer window does not decode (a stored one is installed as failed, and the control plane refuses a change that makes one), and the schema says the same.
guards: model:DecisionTest#a rate limit spec is bounded
spi:RateLimitTest#initWhenTheWindowArithmeticWouldOverflow

rules.source: RFC 0005 §5.1, RFC 0006 §5.3.1 (round 2 review of host and tools, M2)
rules.statement: An http action no request can have does not compile, in a statement, a rate limit rule or the short-form action of a catalog entry (as RoleExpansion.effective writes it out): http:HEAD, since a HEAD request is decided as GET (PIP-18), and an http verb holding an ASCII lower-case letter, since a method that holds one is refused before any decision. The message names the action and says to write http:GET, or the verb in upper case. http:*, upper-case verbs and the verbs of other services stay valid. The data plane and the control plane compile with the one compiler, so a stored document with such an action is installed as failed, and the control plane refuses a change that makes one; the schema says the same.
guards: engine:PolicyCompilerTest#an http action no request can have does not compile

rules.statement: An eq or prefix with ignoreCase whose literal holds a character beyond ASCII that has another case does not compile where a miss lets a request through: in a DENY statement's condition under an even number of nots, in an ALLOW statement's condition under an odd number, in a rate limit rule's condition as in a DENY, and in a policy condition in both directions its statements give it (under an even number of nots when the policy has a DENY, under an odd number when it has an ALLOW). The fold is ASCII only, so such an atom matches fewer spellings than it reads. The message names a spelling the fold misses and says to list every spelling in an in (eq) or an or of prefixes (prefix), without ignoreCase. In the other direction the atom only narrows: it compiles, and the control plane's validation reports a WARNING. cosec-migrate refuses the same shape with the same message.
guards: model:ConditionLintsTest#ignoreCase on a letter beyond ASCII refuses where a miss lets a request through
model:ConditionLintsTest#the direction flips under each not and is kept by and and or
engine:PolicyCompilerTest#ignoreCase beyond ASCII does not compile in the DENY direction

rules.statement: No attribute reference of a document resolves resource.attributes.<name> (a condition operand on either side, a rate limit key): nothing on the request path, in a check, or in the control plane's simulate and explain gives a resource attributes, so a DENY on one would deny nothing. The message says to put facts about a resource in its id and read them with a pattern variable. The policy test kit refuses a scenario that sets request.resource.attributes, for the same reason.
guards: model:ConditionCheckerTest#resource attributes are refused wherever they are referred to
engine:PolicyCompilerTest#resource attributes do not compile
testkit:StrictInputTest#a scenario that sets resource attributes is refused

rules.source: RFC 0004 §4.2, RFC 0009 (IDN-12) (usability review before RC1, UD-3)
rules.statement: A subject.id literal beginning with ( (in eq, in or prefix, in any direction) and a principal binding whose principal id begins with ( do not compile. The anonymous principal has no subject.id in a document and matches no principal binding (BND-4), and no signed-in principal has a reserved id (IDN-12), so such a comparison never holds (and under a not holds for every anonymous request), and such a binding never applies. The message names subject.authenticated. Tenant ids beginning with ( stay valid.
guards: model:ConditionLintsTest#a subject id literal beginning with a parenthesis refuses in every direction
engine:PolicyCompilerTest#a reserved subject id literal does not compile
document:PolicyDocumentCompilerTest#no principal binding names a reserved id

rules.statement: An id a document defines that a route escape names (a policy id, a rate limit rule id) reaches a host's log line and the control plane's ROUTES finding only escaped: a control character or an unpaired surrogate is written as its \uXXXX escape (Identifiers.printable), and each part longer than 128 characters is cut, never inside a surrogate pair, saying how long it was. No document forges a log line on the hosts that install it.
guards: document:RouteEscapesTest#an id that would forge a line is shown escaped, and a long one cut
control:RouteFindingsTest#an id that would forge a line is shown escaped
spring-boot:RouteEscapeReviewTest#an id that would forge a line is logged escaped

rules.source: RC1-15, RC1-52 (RFC 0004 §4.1); review round 1 of beta.4 (R1B-3)
rules.statement: No id a document writes holds a control character or an unpaired surrogate (Identifiers.isUnprintableAt, the rule app and tenant ids follow): policy ids and statement names, binding ids, a binding's subject (principal, role, tenant), app, space and policy, the boundary a document names, role ids with their app, space and listed permissions, catalog permission ids, the external attributes the platform declares, the attribute paths a condition or a rate limit key reads, and pattern variable names. A document holding one does not compile, and the error shows it escaped; a host fails closed on a stored one, as on any document it cannot compile. The message of a document or a policy that does not compile is itself printable. Display text (a role's or catalog entry's name and description, a catalog group's name) is no id.
guards: model:IdentifiersTest#printable text is what printable gives back unchanged
model:ConditionCheckerTest#no attribute reference resolves a name that would forge a line
engine:HttpPathPatternTest#a variable name holds no control character
document:DocumentIdsTest#every id a tenant document writes is checked
document:DocumentIdsTest#a binding's tenant and a role's app are ids too
document:DocumentIdsTest#an app document's catalog entries and roles, and the platform's boundary and attributes, are checked
document:DocumentIdsTest#an unpaired surrogate is refused, a pair is a character like any other
document:DocumentIdsTest#the message of a document that does not compile forges no line, whatever it quotes
document:DocumentIdFieldsTest#every id field of the format is refused at its path when it holds a control character
control:DocumentRefusalHttpTest#a change with a deny matching the path undecoded or an id that would forge a line stays a draft naming it

rules.statement: A DENY statement, and a rate limit rule, whose http resource pattern sets decodeAndParseSegments false does not compile: it matches the path as received, percent-encoded, and would miss every encoded spelling of what it names (a DENY on /admin/** would not stop /%61dmin/users). The error names the statement by its path in the document. An ALLOW keeps the option.
guards: engine:PolicyCompilerTest#a deny that matches the path undecoded does not compile, an allow does
document:PolicyDocumentCompilerTest#a deny matching the path as received does not compile, and the error names the statement
control:DocumentRefusalHttpTest#a change with a deny matching the path undecoded or an id that would forge a line stays a draft naming it
migrate:ConverterTest#a 7x deny matching the path undecoded is rejected at its statement, an allow converts
